title: Harsha's Empire
capsule: Harsha (Harshavardhana, r. 606–647 CE) built a large empire centered on Kanauj in the Gangetic plain after inheriting his brother Rajyavardhana's kingdom of Thanesar and avenging his assassination. By 612 he had consolidated control across most of northern India from the Punjab to Bengal, and the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang, who visited the court in 636, left detailed accounts of the administration, Buddhist patronage, and lavish charitable assemblies (prayaga). Harsha's attempt to expand south of the Narmada was repelled by the Chalukya king Pulakesi II around 618–619, establishing the Narmada as the de facto southern limit. The empire disintegrated immediately after Harsha's death in 647 CE, with his minister Arjuna briefly seizing Kanauj before Tang envoy Wang Xuance intervened.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The approximate extent of Harsha's realm is attested through Xuanzang's travelogue and contemporaneous inscriptions, but provincial boundaries within the empire and the exact eastern frontier are not precisely documented.
